summary: Nora's background passes were thinking themselves out of their own answers; they now answer instead.
details: The model she reads conversations with was set to deliberate before replying. Deliberation is charged against the same budget as the answer, so on a real room it spent the whole budget thinking and produced nothing at all — and on a small one it thought its way to 'I found nothing' about text that plainly contained things to find.
Measured on a real room that had produced nothing for hours: with deliberation on, the call did not return; with it off, three claims in a fraction of the budget.
Turning it off is now a setting the background work owns. What she says in conversation is unaffected — that keeps its own, unchanged.

Giving the background more room was tested and is the wrong fix: at eight times the budget the model spent seven thousand tokens writing the same eleven hundred characters. The cost was deliberation, not space.
limitations: One of the three background passes gets slightly less right without deliberation: asked whether two spellings of a name are the same thing, it now says 'keep them apart' about one time in four where it used to say 'same thing'. That is the safer mistake and the one the design asks for — two names wrongly kept apart is a missing connection, two wrongly merged is a record that has absorbed both and cannot be untangled.

The pass that checks claims against sources still reaches for the web as often as it did, which was the risk worth measuring: one that stopped looking things up would quietly never confirm anything. What has NOT been measured is whether its verdicts are as good, which needs real traffic rather than a probe.
